_note: Past meetings in plain language, newest first. Sourced from district minutes/agendas (Simbli); curated by hand. HTML allowed in item text: <a href="https://...">, b, i, em only.

meetings.record_note: No minutes posted yet — this recap reflects the agenda (the plan), not the vote record.

items.title: Bond contracts — about $83K
items.why: Five consent items moved the first real bond money: cargo storage ($34,000), EOC pad ($13,000), perimeter survey ($8,000), septic risers ($12,000), and cistern/garden water overflow ($16,000).

items.title: Field trips (consent)
items.why: Routine approvals for upcoming student trips.

items.title: William's Law quarterly reports
items.why: The state's school-safety reporting requirement — quarterly confirmation the district is current.

items.title: The three-minute meeting
items.why: Convened 8:49 AM, adjourned 8:52 AM. One substantive act:

items.title: 2025-26 unaudited actuals approved (unanimous)
items.why: The district's closed books for 2025-26, headed to the county office. The full report runs about a hundred pages; the headline numbers are on the budget page — including an attendance shortfall worth roughly $160K in state funding.

items.title: Nine approvals, every vote unanimous
items.why: A two-and-a-half-hour workhorse session: consent agenda plus eight action items, all passing without a dissenting vote.

items.title: Money items
items.why: LCAP revisions, unaudited actuals, the Gann limit (the state's spending cap), and substitute teacher compensation — all approved.

items.title: Facilities and energy
items.why: PCO Energy Resiliency Project, a PG&E contract, and a new facilities fee schedule — all approved.

items.title: New math pilot
items.why: Innovamat Thinking Math approved for piloting.

items.title: The bond pipeline
items.why: $17M in identified project needs; $1M–$2.5M potentially bond-fundable; committee phases finalized, due January 2027.

items.title: People
items.why: New special-education and custodial hires start in October. Closed session covered union negotiations (CSEA and HUTA), anticipated litigation, and the superintendent's review.

items.title: What's coming
items.why: Parcel tax discussions (Koslen), a Town Hall on October 15, and new-board-member training January 14.

items.title: One quiet hour with the lawyer
items.why: Almost the entire meeting was closed session: legal counsel on two anticipated litigation matters. No report out, no votes, no dollars. The public record is essentially "we met with our lawyer."
